findings.reason: the bound must be re-set below base's measured 26 s (or the freshness figure taken from a call base demonstrably exceeds) or §24 can never show the repairs buy anything, and the false "must fail" claim would otherwise ship a node that stalls on its own control.
findings.text: §24 sets the head target "the second forced sweep's median on the GPFS copy is under 30 s" and asserts "the same bound applied to base must fail", but the same paragraph cites §20's own figure, "the steady derivation at about 26 s at base on both filesystems"; §20 measured exactly the revision §24 uses as base (main before §21 merged) and reported steady-state medians of 26.0 s GPFS / 26.2 s node-local, and §18 records that a sweep costs fleet_state plus only 0.135 s of slicing and writes, so base's second forced sweep is about 26 s — under the 30 s bound. The bound therefore holds whether or not §21–§23 landed, and §24's own fallback ("If base already meets it, the bound cannot discriminate the repairs, and the node reports that rather than passing") makes the section un-completable as the validation it was written to be.
